value.text:
Fifteen seasons in San Francisco, and nobody on a card has made more tackles.

K'Lavon Settle has played 255 games for the 49ers since Y73 and made 3,185 tackles, about twelve and a half every time he takes the field. He has intercepted 36 passes. He has never been credited with a sack or a forced fumble, because his job was never to gamble. He reads the play, closes the distance and brings the ball carrier down, snap after snap, season after season.

He has done it without a ring and without an individual award. What he has instead is the deepest tackle total the league has seen, and he is still adding to it.

He arrives in the Y87 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. K'Lavon Settle, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Eight seasons, seven rings, and the best rushing seasons the record board has ever seen.

Ryland Maxwell came into the league with the Jets in Y80 and was Rookie of the Year, winning titles in Y80 and Y82. When Dorren Skura left for Atlanta after Y82, Maxwell went with him, and the Falcons have won every season since: Y83, Y84, Y85, Y86 and Y87.

In 156 games he has carried the ball 2,027 times for 15,141 yards and 211 touchdowns, and caught 111 passes for 817 yards and 32 more. He owns the single-game rushing record at 237 yards, the single-season touchdown record at 39 and the single-season yardage record at 2,670, set in Y87. Two Offensive Player of the Year awards and three Super Bowl MVPs say he saves his best for the biggest stage.

Ryland Maxwell, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him.

Kalif Suh has played 229 games and made 705 tackles, with 17 interceptions, 21 sacks and 10 forced fumbles. That is a linebacker who does a little of everything: about three tackles a game, a takeaway when an offense gets careless, and pressure when the call comes to go get the quarterback.

He won three rings in New York, in Y77, Y80 and Y82, all on Dorren Skura's teams. When Skura left for Atlanta, Suh stayed, and he has kept the Jets defense steady ever since.

He arrives under the higher bar of Career Legacy 7,500, the second player inducted under it after Juwann Gilman. Kalif Suh, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them.

He has played 299 games and carried the ball 2,805 times for 20,416 yards, better than seven yards a carry, with 367 rushing touchdowns. He catches it too: 235 receptions for 1,871 yards and 60 more scores. Two Offensive Player of the Year awards say the league noticed.

It started in Tennessee, where he was Rookie of the Year on the Titans team that won it all in Y72. Seattle came next, then the Jets, where he won a second ring in Y77 and ran for 212 yards in a single game in Y78, a record that stood until Y85. Four seasons in Atlanta followed, and then the road led back to New York, where he is still carrying the ball.

Malakai Sawyer, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
